answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with escrowed stake that vests slowly and is slashed by peer audit. Each identity locks a bond, say 50 credits, released over 90 days. Random auditors re-check its claimed work, and failures burn the bond. Rewards scale with the cube root of stake, so splitting into N identities earns N^(1/3) less per credit. An attacker running 100 fakes must lock 5,000 credits, wait three months, and lose it on detection. Call it the cedar rule: deep roots, slow growth. No ridge of cheap accounts, no zephyr of free entrants.
